hook: Paul Werbos studied economics at the London School of Economics before earning a PhD from Harvard University in 1974, where his dissertation, Beyond Regression, described how the chain rule for ordered derivatives could train neural network-like models, work later recognized as the first description of backpropagation. Through the 1980s he worked as an econometric forecasting analyst at the U.S. Energy Information Administration, applying related statistical modeling techniques. In 1988 he joined the National Science Foundation as a program director, where he spent over two decades directing funding for research on adaptive systems and neural networks before retiring in 2015. His dissertation was later republished as the book The Roots of Backpropagation (Wiley, 1994), and he went on to develop related ideas under the name adaptive dynamic programming, connecting neural networks with dynamic programming based control. In 2011 the International Neural Network Society gave him its Hebb Award, its highest honor.

quick_facts: Described the chain rule for ordered derivatives, the mathematical basis of backpropagation, in his 1974 Harvard PhD dissertation.
His dissertation was republished as the book The Roots of Backpropagation (Wiley, 1994).
Also developed adaptive dynamic programming, linking neural networks with dynamic programming based control methods.
Worked as an econometric forecasting analyst at the U.S. Energy Information Administration from 1980 to 1989.
Served as a National Science Foundation program director from 1988 until his retirement in 2015.
Received the International Neural Network Society's Hebb Award in 2011 and is a Fellow of IEEE.

achievements.title: First description of backpropagation (1974)
achievements.impact: His Harvard PhD dissertation, Beyond Regression, described the chain rule for ordered derivatives applied to training neural network-like models, years before backpropagation became standard in machine learning.

achievements.title: The Roots of Backpropagation (Wiley, 1994)
achievements.impact: Republished his dissertation as a book, documenting the mathematical foundations of the algorithm that now underlies most deep learning training.

achievements.title: Adaptive dynamic programming
achievements.impact: Developed methods combining neural networks with dynamic programming for approximate optimal control, influencing later reinforcement learning research.

achievements.title: National Science Foundation program director (1988-2015)
achievements.impact: Directed funding across adaptive systems and neural network research programs for more than two decades.
